proposedOverrides.name: Accomac communities
proposedOverrides.summary: Indigenous Accomac communities occupied Virginia’s southern Eastern Shore, farming, fishing and exchanging goods across its creeks and coastal landscapes.

identityAssessment.finding: The imported 1492 polygon lies on the lower Virginia Eastern Shore, approximately 76.02 to 75.72 degrees west and 37.21 to 37.64 degrees north. It is interpreted as the Indigenous Accomac label, not the modern town of Belle Haven linked by the imported summary. The override clarifies the name without changing the polygon or interval. No precise 1492 frontier is certified.

scopeNotes: DHR marker gives the first patent as 1640 and the Library of Virginia as 1641; approximate wording retains the disagreement.
The Library of Virginia 2024 biography corrects the composite Debedeavon/Laughing King story repeated by older works and some heritage pages.
No excavated house or object is invented to satisfy a quota; documentary examples and qualified archaeological associations supply the evidence.
